📌 Rule / Concept: Infinitive Construction in Passive (Object + to-infinitive)

When an active sentence follows the structure: Subject + reporting verb (expect, believe, consider, want, order, allow, etc.) + object + to-verb, it can be converted into passive by making the object the subject, followed by the appropriate form of “be” + V³, while the infinitive remains unchanged. The correct passive structure becomes: Object + be + V³ + to + V¹.

Here, “expects” is the reporting verb, “the compliance team” is the object, and “to submit” is the infinitive.

In passive voice, the object (“the compliance team”) becomes the subject. Therefore, the correct structure is:

“The compliance team is expected to submit the revised report by Monday.”

🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

Identify the object before the infinitive. Make that object the subject in passive. Keep the infinitive in base form (to + V¹). Do not unnecessarily convert it into “to be + V³” unless meaning demands it. This structure is frequently tested with verbs like expect, believe, consider, report, and suppose in Banking and SSC Mains examinations.

When “make” is used as a causative verb in active voice, it follows the structure:

Certain verbs such as give, offer, send, tell, award, lend, promise, etc., take two objects:

Structure 2 (Direct Object as Subject):
Direct Object + be + V³ + to + Indirect Object

When the active sentence contains an indefinite subject such as someone, somebody, people, they, etc., the subject is usually omitted in passive voice because it is either unknown or unimportant. The object becomes the subject, and the verb changes according to the tense.

The structure “get + V³” is known as the get-passive. It is commonly used in informal English and often emphasizes that the subject was affected by the action. However, in formal written English (and in competitive exams), the standard passive form uses:

Subject + be (appropriate tense) + V³

Thus, “got promoted” corresponds to “was promoted” in standard passive structure.

The employee was promoted after demonstrating exceptional leadership skills.
